title: Burrowing Owl — AI upsizing
subtitle: A small Burrowing Owl capture (1954 × 1466) run through six 2× upsamplers and four 4× variants. Compare any pair side-by-side at native pixel resolution to see how much real detail each tool reconstructs vs. how much is plausible-looking confabulation.
exif_summary: OM-1MarkII with OM 150-400mm F4.5 TC at 500mm (1002mm equivalent), 1/1000s at f/5.6, ISO 640

images.title: RAW
images.caption: Original RAW image, cropped toby 1466 pixels

critique.text: The original, un-upscaled RAW crop. As a heavily cropped image, it lacks resolution and displays visible noise and softness. Summary comparison: Topaz AI tools (particularly Gigapixel High Fidelity at 2x) consistently outperformed ON1 by successfully generating realistic, crisp feather details, whereas ON1 produced softer, mushier results, especially at 4x. Lightroom Super Resolution offered a solid, conservative middle ground—clean and free of AI artifacts, but lacking the impressive detail recovery of the Topaz models.

images.title: Topaz Gigapixel 2x High Fidelity
images.caption: Topaz Gigapixel 2x with High Fidelity model, recommended settings

critique.text: Upscaled using Topaz Gigapixel 2x (High Fidelity model). This is arguably the most successful image in the set. The 2x magnification combined with the High Fidelity model finds the perfect sweet spot. It produces remarkably natural, crisp feather detail without over-sharpening or introducing artificial 'plasticky' textures. The transition between the sharp subject and smooth background is flawlessly maintained.

Upscaled using Lightroom Super Resolution at 2x. This provides a very clean, conservative baseline for upscaling. It retains the natural character of the original RAW file without introducing any 'waxy' or 'crunchy' AI artifacts. While it doesn't artificially generate the breathtaking fine feather detail seen in the Topaz 2x High Fidelity version, it is a highly reliable, artifact-free result that is superior to ON1.

images.title: Topaz Gigapixel 2x standard
images.caption: Topaz Gigapixel 2x with standard model, recommended settings

critique.text: Upscaled using Topaz Gigapixel 2x (Standard model). A strong result, but when compared directly to the High Fidelity 2x version, it falls slightly short. The feather textures look a little bit more clumpy and less organically fine. It's a very usable image, but the Standard model shows a hint of that characteristic AI 'smoothing' on the microscopic level.

images.title: Topaz Photo 2x Low Resolution
images.caption: Upscaled using Topaz Photo 2x, with recommended Low Resolution model and default settings

critique.text: Upscaled using Topaz Photo 2x with the Low Resolution model. This approach yields excellent, crisp detail recovery. The Low Res model effectively handles the noise of the original crop and generates plausible feather textures. While slightly aggressive in its rendering of the finest micro-details, giving it a faintly 'processed' look upon close inspection, it is a highly effective and impactful upscale.

images.title: Topaz Gigapixel 4x high fidelity
images.caption: Topaz Gigapixel 4x with high fidelity model, recommended settings

critique.text: Upscaled using Topaz Gigapixel 4x (High Fidelity, default settings). This image shows incredible detail generation for a 4x upscale, significantly outperforming ON1's 4x attempt. However, leaving the sharpness at default makes the feathers look slightly crunchy and introduces minor halos along high-contrast edges compared to the reduced-sharpness version (Image 5). It is impressive but slightly over-cooked.

images.title: Topaz Gigapixel 4x high fidelty reduced sharpness
images.caption: Topaz Gigapixel 4x with high fidelty model, sharpness setting reduced from 78 to 39

critique.text: Upscaled using Topaz Gigapixel 4x (High Fidelity, reduced sharpness). Dialing back the sharpness on the High Fidelity model was a smart choice here. It achieves an impressive 4x enlargement without succumbing to the brittle, over-sharpened look that often plagues extreme AI upscaling. The feather details are organic and well-defined, making it the most successful 4x upscale in this set.

images.title: ON1 Resize AI 2x High Quality with screen sharpening
images.caption: ON1 Resize AI 2x High Quality, screen sharpening with default settings

critique.text: Upsized using ON1 Resize AI at 2x with screen sharpening. This is a noticeable improvement over the 4x ON1 attempt, retaining more realistic structure. However, the screen sharpening introduces slight edge harshness without truly recovering the fine, distinct feather details that the AI models from Topaz managed to find. It feels like a traditional upscale with a strong unsharp mask applied.

images.title: Topaz Gigapixel 4x Standard
images.caption: Topaz Gigapixel 4x with standard model, recommended settings

critique.text: Upscaled using Topaz Gigapixel 4x (Standard model). The Standard model struggles slightly with natural textures like feathers compared to the High Fidelity model. While sharp, the details take on a slightly waxy, 'painterly', or artificial quality, typical of AI hallucinating textures it doesn't quite understand perfectly. It's better than ON1's mushiness, but less natural than Gigapixel's High Fidelity output.

images.title: ON1 Resize AI 2x High Quality
images.caption: ON1 Resize AI 2x High Quality, no sharpening

critique.text: Upsized using ON1 Resize AI at 2x with no sharpening. Without the artificial sharpening, the soft, somewhat muddy nature of the ON1 upscaling algorithm is very apparent. While free of ringing artifacts, it completely lacks the micro-contrast and fine feather detail necessary for a compelling wildlife portrait, rendering it distinctly inferior to the Topaz and Lightroom results.

images.title: ON1 Resize AI 4x High Quality with screen sharpening
images.caption: ON1 Resize AI 4x High Quality, screen sharpening with default settings

critique.text: Upsized using ON1 Resize AI at 4x with screen sharpening. The 4x magnification has pushed this software beyond its limits for detail recovery. The image is noticeably soft and mushy, with feather textures appearing painted or blurred rather than naturally resolved. It lacks the crispness seen in the Topaz alternatives, showing that ON1 struggles with extreme upscaling on heavily cropped files.
